s1.syndrome_frame: Upper gastrointestinal bleeding with a gastric mass and anemia
salient_findings: Heterogeneous mass with fat attenuation and internal septations on CT
key_facts: Approximately 1 year of upper gastrointestinal bleeding
No prior evaluations
Referred for upper endoscopy
Large antral mass found on endoscopy
Mucosal biopsy was obtained
Declined endoscopic ultrasound initially
Lost to follow-up during pregnancy
Returned with ongoing anemia and new epigastric pain
Repeat esophagogastroduodenoscopy with endoscopic ultrasound identified a 6 cm mass
Mass arose from the muscularis propria of the gastric antrum
CT demonstrated a 9.7 × 7.8 × 4.8 cm heterogeneous mass
Mass was adherent to the posterior wall of the gastric antrum
Mass had predominantly fat attenuation and internal septations
No pathologic lymphadenopathy
Presented with melena
Biopsy results were consistent with adipose tissue

shortlist.label: Lipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass had predominantly fat attenuation and biopsy results were consistent with adipose tissue

shortlist.label: Liposarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Large antral mass with heterogeneous appearance and internal septations on CT

shortlist.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Mass arose from the muscularis propria of the gastric antrum

shortlist.label: Leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass arose from the muscularis propria of the gastric antrum and had a large size

shortlist.label: Myolipoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mass had predominantly fat attenuation and arose from the muscularis propria of the gastric antrum

raw.rationale: The mass had predominantly fat attenuation and internal septations on CT, and biopsy results were consistent with adipose tissue, which are characteristic features of a lipoma.

rejected.label: Liposarcoma
rejected.why: Liposarcomas are typically more aggressive and would likely have shown pathologic lymphadenopathy or more rapid growth.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rejected.why: GISTs do not typically have fat attenuation on imaging and often have a more solid appearance.

rejected.label: Leiomyoma
rejected.why: Leiomyomas are smooth muscle tumors and would not have the characteristic fat attenuation seen on imaging.

rejected.label: Myolipoma
rejected.why: While myolipomas do contain adipose tissue, they are less common in the stomach and the clinical presentation and imaging findings are more consistent with a lipoma.
